tyrannical

tih-RAN-ih-kul -- from tyrant / tyranny + -ical. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

To be tyrannical is to be cruel and harsh in the use of power.

The tyrannical warlord taxed the villagers into poverty while living in extravagant luxury himself.

Example

History remembers the emperor as tyrannical: he executed rivals without trial, silenced any criticism, and ruled purely by fear rather than law.

Tyrannical describes the cruel, oppressive use of power -- not just having power, but abusing it harshly and unfairly over people who have no way to resist.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

oppressive: Oppressive describes harsh, unjust control that weighs people down -- oppressive laws, an oppressive workload. Tyrannical points at the ruler: a tyrannical figure uses power cruelly and personally, while oppressive can describe a system's weight with no single villain named.

autocratic: Autocratic means holding all the decision-making power alone -- no votes, no consultation. It says nothing about cruelty: an autocratic manager can be perfectly fair. Tyrannical adds the cruelty; it is about how harshly power is used, not just who holds it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

benevolent: kind and well-meaning in the use of power

just: fair and reasonable

Where it sits · how oppressive the control is — strict → tyrannical → despotic

strict vs. tyrannical: Strict sits at the mild end of this scale: firm, demanding rules, fairly enforced -- a strict teacher is not a villain. Tyrannical is a different order of severity: power used cruelly and unjustly against people who cannot resist.

despotic vs. tyrannical: Despotic goes a step beyond tyrannical: it keeps all of tyrannical's cruelty and adds total, unchecked control -- a single ruler answering to no law at all.

Put it together

Put it together: Tyrannical comes from tyrant/tyranny -- from Greek tyrannos, 'sole ruler' -- plus -ical. Tyrannical describes the cruel, oppressive use of power over people who have no way to resist.
